and

and, a connective particle, as καί [and] is conjunctive: see Hermann, Opuscula vol. 3 p. 835. Wellauer diligently collected the Aeschylean examples, which I have placed below, correcting what needed correction.
1. τε [and] joining single words.
2. τε [and] answering to a following καί [and].
3. τε [and] joining periods and parts of periods.
4. Regarding the placement of the particle, it should be noted that it is very often attached to a preposition, not to the nearest substantive to which it pertains.
